title: Sore throat (pharyngitis)

items: Pharyngitis is inflammation of the throat, most often from a virus.
Some sore throats are caused by a strep (group A streptococcus) infection, which needs antibiotics.
Sore throat, fever, and tender glands in the front of the neck.
White patches or swelling of the tonsils. Cough and runny nose point more towards a virus.
A rapid antigen test (RADT) or a throat swab culture.
Your doctor may use the Centor score (a list of 4 points) to decide if testing is needed.
Antibiotics are used only when a strep infection is likely or confirmed. Your doctor will decide.
Ask your doctor or pharmacist about pain relief.

sections.h: What you can do at home
items: Drink warm fluids, and rest your voice.
Stay away from others until the fever has settled.
See your doctor if you are not better after a few days, or if symptoms come back.
This leaflet gives general information. Follow your doctor's advice.

urgent: The source entry lists no specific emergency sign for this condition.
Get urgent help if you have trouble breathing or swallowing, or feel suddenly much worse.
